lessons: A directory-name-based parent check (processed_*_*, *_visualized_id_NN) is a more durable defense than an ever-growing filename-suffix list -- it catches future overlay-writing tools the suffix list hasn't been updated for yet, which is exactly the bug class being fixed here.

vaila_sapiens.py already has its own, separate, more robust _is_sapiens_derived_video() (parent-directory-based: 'any parent named processed_sapiens_*') -- it was not affected by this bug because it never shared sam3sapiens2.py's helper. Worth remembering as prior art next time a similar filter needs auditing.

A 'wrong' directory can still contain a real, useful predictions JSON (sam3sapiens2_visualize.py copies source_artifacts) -- rejecting it purely because the caller supplied the wrong video_stem is overly rigid once _find_videos() itself no longer supplies that wrong stem. Informs the design of ranked target (b).

The predictions JSON only stores the raw video's bare filename (payload['video'] = video_path.name), never an absolute path -- full auto-fill of an exact path is not possible from the JSON alone. Walking upward from the results directory (a few levels) to find a uniquely-named match is a reasonable, safe heuristic for the common convention where a processed_*/ batch output sits nested under (or next to) the original raw-input folder; ambiguity (multiple distinct matches) must fall back to 'not found' rather than guess.

The video/payload mismatch check added to _resolve_sapiens2_front_end() is a correctness fix independent of the UX work -- even in the tool's original, fully-correct usage, a user could have pointed -i at a different video than --sapiens2-results was computed from and gotten silently misaligned frame-by-frame guidance with no error. Worth remembering as a class of risk (guidance/results keyed by frame index, not content) whenever wiring a new results-consuming CLI flag in this pipeline family.

Chaining two independently-validated pipelines (sapiens2_3d.py's SAM3D output -> monocular_dlt_align.py's DLT placement) by importing and calling the second one's own public function unmodified, per-person, with a caught-and-logged exception per person, is a low-risk integration pattern: a failure in one person's placement cannot take down the other four, and the underlying SAM3D CSVs the chain reads are already safely on disk regardless of whether the chain runs at all.

One person's reprojection error (person 2, 3.31 px vs the ~1 px others) tracked directly to the same small/distant bbox flagged as suspicious back in the pipeline loop's own tier-3 smoke test -- cross-referencing an earlier loop's recorded caveats against new real-data evidence is a cheap, worthwhile sanity check before treating an outlier as a bug.

For a 631-frame real GPU run with 5 tracked people, wiring the DLT-chain in-process (called once per person from inside the same Python process that already holds the SAM3D output) is cheap enough (~1 minute total for all 5 placements) that it does not need its own subprocess isolation -- unlike sapiens2_3d.py's own SAM3D stage, a placement failure here does not risk CUDA/VRAM corruption since the chain itself is CPU-only linear algebra.
